# `kernel/RuleGraph.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/RuleGraph.js`

RuleGraph.js — declarative capability-based permissions engine. Rules are evaluated in registration order; the LAST matching rule wins (CSS-like specificity — more specific rules override general ones). Capabilities follow a dot-namespace convention: fs.read, fs.write, gpu.compute, gpu.acquireSurface, net.send, net.on, ai.infer, ui.notify, ipc.emit, … Wildcard matching: 'fs.*'  matches any capability starting with 'fs.' '*'     matches everything Condition functions receive (appId, capability, manifest) and return bool. A rule with a condition is only applied when the condition is true. Usage: const graph = new RuleGraph() .allow('fs.*') .deny('net.*') .allowIf('gpu.compute', (id, cap, mf) => mf.permissions?.includes('gpu.compute')); const { granted, reason } = graph.check('os.calculator', 'fs.read', manifest);

## Classes

### `class RuleGraph`

RuleGraph.js — declarative capability-based permissions engine. Rules are evaluated in registration order; the LAST matching rule wins (CSS-like specificity — more specific rules override general ones). Capabilities follow a dot-namespace convention: fs.read, fs.write, gpu.compute, gpu.acquireSurface, net.send, net.on, ai.infer, ui.notify, ipc.emit, … Wildcard matching: 'fs.*'  matches any capability starting with 'fs.' '*'     matches everything Condition functions receive (appId, capability, manifest) and return bool. A rule with a condition is only applied when the condition is true. Usage: const graph = new RuleGraph() .allow('fs.*') .deny('net.*') .allowIf('gpu.compute', (id, cap, mf) => mf.permissions?.includes('gpu.compute')); const { granted, reason } = graph.check('os.calculator', 'fs.read', manifest);

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor()` |  |
| `allow` | `allow(capability, appIds = '*', reason = '')` | Allow `capability` for `appIds` (string, array, or '*' for all). |
| `deny` | `deny(capability, appIds = '*', reason = '')` | Deny `capability` for `appIds`. |
| `allowIf` | `allowIf(capability, conditionFn, reason = '')` | Allow `capability` for all apps where `conditionFn(appId, capability, manifest)` returns true. |
| `denyIf` | `denyIf(capability, conditionFn, reason = '')` | Deny `capability` for all apps where `conditionFn(appId, capability, manifest)` returns true. |
| `check` | `check(appId, capability, manifest = {})` | Evaluate the rule graph for an app+capability pair. |
| `checkAll` | `checkAll(appId, capabilities, manifest = {})` | Check many capabilities at once. |
| `grantedCaps` | `grantedCaps(appId, manifest = {}, knownCaps = KNOWN_CAPABILITIES)` | Return all capabilities that an app is currently granted (from the registered rule set). Only works for the known set of `knownCaps` you pass in. |
| `dump` | `dump()` |  |

## Functions

### `buildDefaultRuleGraph()`

Build the default OS-wide RuleGraph. Apps with explicit manifest.permissions entries unlock restricted capabilities.

## Constants

- `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
- `CAPABILITY_LABELS` — Human-readable label for each capability (used by PermissionPortal).

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
